//: The answer sheet for the size fields' client-side refusals (#830).
The SERVER grades it: tests/quota/test_item_size_parity.py asserts `max_*` equal GET /environment's,
and every row's `accepted` is the PUT's 200/422 on `sent` — or on `typed`, where the client would not
send at all (`sent: null`), so a client refusal is never one the server would have accepted.
The CLIENT is graded against it: web/tests/itemSizeParity.test.ts asserts cpuFault/memoryFault(typed, max)
is null iff `accepted`, and that Number(typed) / normaliseMemory(typed) is `sent`.
A bound copied into the client would drift with every test green; a sheet the server marks cannot.
Update it by re-reading the server, never by hand — the python test fails on a stale ceiling first,
and once that is corrected names every row whose verdict moved.
